name: DISA STIG, SSH server (Oracle Linux 8)
reference: CIS Oracle Linux 8 STIG Benchmark v1.0.0, the SSH rules requiring FIPS-validated ciphers, MACs and key exchange (verified against /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config). Each audit fails a server whose configuration lists anything other than the named list, so this profile is an allowlist of those three lists.
summary: The US Department of Defense hardening for SSH on Oracle Linux 8: a FIPS 140-2 allowlist of ciphers, MACs and key exchange set through the system crypto-policies. Its mandated lists coincide with the RHEL 8 STIG's -- keeping aes192-ctr and a seven-method key exchange -- but this is the Oracle Linux 8 document, cited and versioned on its own.
notes: One profile per STIG document. Oracle Linux 8 is a RHEL 8-compatible distribution, and its STIG's mandated SSH lists coincide with the RHEL 8 STIG's: ciphers aes256-ctr, aes192-ctr, aes128-ctr, aes256-gcm@openssh.com, aes128-gcm@openssh.com (five, keeping aes192-ctr, unlike the RHEL 9 line); MACs the four HMAC-SHA-2 in plain and encrypt-then-MAC form; and a key-exchange rule of the three NIST ECDH curves, diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256, and the SHA-2 MODP groups 14, 16 and 18. It configures these through /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config, but the tool measures what the server offers on the wire, which is what the allowlist governs. It is a distinct document from the RHEL 8 STIG, so a distinct profile. Lists taken from audit/remediation, not Default Value.

cipher.reason: The Oracle Linux 8 STIG cipher rule's audit fails a server offering anything other than these five; the remediation sets exactly them.

mac.reason: The Oracle Linux 8 STIG MAC rule's audit fails a server offering anything other than these four FIPS-validated MACs.

kex.reason: The Oracle Linux 8 STIG key-exchange rule's audit fails a server offering anything other than these seven FIPS-validated methods.
